title: Florisbad spring site and hominin cranium (South Africa)
summary: Florisbad is a thermal-spring site in South Africa's Free State where T. F. Dreyer found a partial hominin skull in 1932, named Homo helmei. An electron spin resonance date on an associated tooth gave about 259,000 years, but the tooth-skull link and the age are disputed.

uncertainty.note: ESR date 259 +/- 35 ka on a tooth presumed to belong to the skull (Grün et al. 1996, as reported by Hawks); the association and age are contested. The skull was found in 1932.

as_recorded.calendar: Years before present, ESR on tooth enamel

as_recorded.value: 1932, by Dreyer during his Florisbad excavations

when.display: c. 259,000 years ago (ESR, disputed); skull found 1932

where.modern_name: Florisbad, near Bloemfontein, Free State, South Africa
where.historical_name: Spring and salt pan in the interior highveld of southern Africa, Middle Pleistocene; no polities exist at this date

importance.justification: Among the oldest candidate Homo sapiens-lineage fossils in Africa, though its age is contested.

sources.title: Dreyer, Prof Thomas Francis (Biographical Database of Southern African Science)

sources.title: How old is the "early Homo sapiens" skull from Florisbad?
sources.publisher: John Hawks (University of Wisconsin-Madison paleoanthropologist, personal site)

reviewer_note: Least sure of the age: the 259 ka ESR date rests on a tooth-skull association that Berger and Hawks dispute. S2A3 describes the site as a salt pan north-east of Bloemfontein; Wikidata gives the pin. Hawks is a personal site (class other).
